findings.title: macOS is entirely absent from CI, leaving all macOS-specific loader code unexercised
findings.description: The matrix arch dimension is ["ubuntu-latest", "ubuntu-24.04-arm", "windows-latest"] (numbduck_ci.yml:22); there is no macOS runner in any workflow (haversine_bench.yml:14 is also Linux-only). Yet numbduck carries a large body of macOS-only code that exists precisely because duckdb-python >=1.4.1 strips the C API on macOS (CLAUDE.md 'macOS C API stripping is intentional'): the standalone-dylib discovery (_find_standalone_libduckdb, utils.py:33-47), the network download fallback with consent gate (_download_libduckdb, utils.py:50-91), the legacy-cache cleanup, the versioned cache keyed on duckdb.__version__, and the double-load of two duckdb runtimes (utils.py:115 wheel + utils.py:121/130 standalone). None of this is run by CI. The struct-by-value SysV x86-64 / ARM64 ABI branches (_call_lib_func_struct_in/out) are validated on Linux, but the macOS-specific library acquisition path — the most failure-prone part of the project per the loader note — has zero automated coverage.
findings.impact: The platform the project documents as its hardest case (symbol-stripped wheel requiring standalone discovery or download) can regress silently. A change to the download URL scheme, cache layout, version-string-to-release-tag mapping, or the double-load runtime interaction would not be caught until a macOS user hits it.
findings.recommendation: Add at least one macos-latest (ARM64) matrix entry that exercises load_duckdb end-to-end, ideally with NUMBDUCK_LIBDUCKDB pointing at a brew-installed libduckdb so the standalone path is hit deterministically without the interactive download. Even a single smoke job materially closes the gap.

findings.title: benchmark marker promises CI deselection but bare pytest runs the 1M-row benchmark in every job
findings.description: pyproject.toml:26 declares the marker as 'benchmark: slow benchmarks, run only locally (deselected in CI)'. Nothing implements that deselection: there is no addopts in pyproject.toml, no conftest.py anywhere in the repo, and the CI test step runs a bare `pytest` (numbduck_ci.yml:76) with no `-m "not benchmark"`. test_udf_benchmark (test/test_ducklib.py:2684, decorated @pytest.mark.benchmark) hard-codes ROW_COUNTS = [10_000, 100_000, 1_000_000] (test_ducklib.py:2703) with no NUMBDUCK_BENCH_BIG gate, and its own docstring records the 1M-row Python scalar path at ~118.8s. So this benchmark executes in full on every CI job, contradicting the marker's documented contract.
findings.impact: Every matrix job pays a multi-minute benchmark cost (the 1M-row Python UDF alone is ~2 minutes per the docstring), multiplied across the large matrix — directly contrary to the comment's stated 'reduce billable minutes' intent elsewhere in the same workflow. The marker is effectively dead/misleading: a reader trusts it is deselected when it is not.
findings.recommendation: Either add `addopts = "-m 'not benchmark'"` under [tool.pytest.ini_options] (then run benchmarks explicitly with `-m benchmark` locally), or change the CI step to `pytest -m "not benchmark"`. Fix the marker description to match whichever mechanism is chosen.

findings.title: Committed __version__ is the empty string, so any non-CI build produces an empty/malformed version
findings.description: Packaging uses dynamic version from an attribute: version = {attr = "numbduck.__version__"} (pyproject.toml:29-30), and the committed numbduck/__init__.py is literally `__version__ = ""`. The meaningful value is injected only by CI's 'Write version to __init__.py' step (numbduck_ci.yml:58-60). A contributor running `python -m build` or `pip install -e .` locally therefore resolves the version to the empty string, with no error. setuptools will emit a wheel with an empty/normalized-to-0.0.0-ish version silently.
findings.impact: Local builds are non-reproducible and silently mis-versioned; a developer cannot produce a correctly-versioned wheel without replicating the CI echo step by hand. The single source of truth lives only in CI YAML, not in the repo.
findings.recommendation: Commit a real fallback version (e.g. `__version__ = "0.0.0.dev0"`) or move version resolution to a tool that reads git metadata (setuptools-scm), so a local build yields a valid PEP 440 version without the CI overwrite.

findings.title: numbox is unpinned during CI installs, making the matrix a time-varying, non-reproducible input
findings.description: The install step pins numba and duckdb to explicit matrix values (`pip install "numba==..."`, `"duckdb==..."`, numbduck_ci.yml:65-66) but installs numbox only transitively via `pip install -e .` (numbduck_ci.yml:67), which resolves numbox~=0.5.11 (pyproject.toml:13) to whatever latest 0.5.x exists at run time. numbduck is built directly on numbox's _call_lib_func / @cres / signatures surface, so a new numbox 0.5.x patch can change CI pass/fail with zero repo change. The same asymmetry appears in haversine_bench.yml, which fully pins numpy/pyarrow/numba/duckdb (haversine_bench.yml:27) but not numbox.
findings.impact: Green CI is not reproducible across time; a numbox release can break (or silently mask) a build, and bisecting a failure cannot distinguish numbduck changes from a floating dependency. Contradicts the otherwise-careful pinning of the rest of the stack.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit `pip install "numbox==<floor>"` (or a small set of numbox versions as a matrix dimension) before the editable install, mirroring the numba/duckdb treatment, so the dependency that numbduck most tightly couples to is the one pinned, not the one left floating.

findings.title: Documented numbox pin (0.5.6) is stale relative to the actual pin (0.5.11)
findings.description: CLAUDE.md:16 ('Key dependencies') states `numbox~=0.5.6`, but the load-bearing pin in pyproject.toml:13 is `numbox~=0.5.11`. ~=0.5.6 means >=0.5.6,<0.6; ~=0.5.11 raises the floor to 0.5.11. The resolver only reads pyproject.toml, so the real build floor is 0.5.11; the documentation (and any reasoning derived from it) understates the floor by five patch releases.
findings.impact: Maintainers/reviewers reasoning from CLAUDE.md will assume numbox 0.5.6 is a supported floor when it is not — a fragile version assumption that masks the real compatibility contract.
findings.recommendation: Update CLAUDE.md:16 to `numbox~=0.5.11` to match pyproject.toml, or, better, have the doc reference the pin location rather than restating the value so it cannot drift again.

findings.title: Windows binding coverage is a single thin slice despite Windows-specific ABI code paths
findings.description: Matrix exclusions (numbduck_ci.yml:30-39) restrict windows-latest to Python 3.11 only and duckdb 1.5.1 only, leaving exactly {3.11} x {numba 0.60.0, 0.64.0} x {1.5.1} = 2 Windows jobs. The Windows struct-by-value ABI branches are materially different from SysV (per CLAUDE.md 'Struct-by-value helpers': _call_lib_func_struct_in passes <=16-byte structs by pointer on Windows, struct_out uses sret, and the intrinsics' byval+optnone handling differs). Those Windows-specific lowering paths are validated against a single Python and a single duckdb version.
findings.impact: A Windows-ABI regression tied to a different Python or duckdb version (or a duckdb floor like 1.3.2 that Windows never runs) would not be caught. The narrowing is deliberate for billable minutes, but it leaves the platform whose ABI diverges most under-covered.
findings.recommendation: Accept the cost tradeoff if intended, but document it explicitly, and consider adding one Windows job at the duckdb floor (1.3.2) so the lower bound of the supported duckdb range is exercised on the divergent ABI at least once.

notes: Scope: pyproject.toml + four workflows + loader/build understanding notes. Highest-impact gaps: (1) macOS — the platform with the most bespoke loader code (standalone discovery, network download fallback, double-runtime load) — has zero CI coverage; (2) the 'benchmark' marker advertises CI deselection that is not implemented, so a ~2-minute 1M-row benchmark runs in every matrix job. python_requires (>=3.10) correctly matches the CI Python span 3.10-3.13 and the duckdb pin range is covered by the 1.3.2/1.4.0/1.5.1 matrix points, so no defect there. numbox~=0.5.11 vs duckdb>=1.3.2,<1.6 pins are themselves reasonable; the reproducibility problem is that numbox is left unpinned at install time while numba/duckdb are pinned.
